question: What is the primary cause of hereditary conditions?
explanation: Hereditary conditions stem directly from genetic mutations or alterations passed down from parents to their offspring. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h1)

question: Why is early identification of genetic risks important for nurses in primary healthcare?

options.A: It prevents patients from developing infectious diseases
options.B: It allows for proactive education and early risk reduction
options.C: It completely cures the genetic condition before birth
options.D: It eliminates the need for any further medical testing

explanation: Spotting risks early gives healthcare providers the chance to guide families and prevent severe complications before symptoms appear. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h1)

question: How many copies of a mutated gene must a child inherit to show symptoms of an autosomal recessive condition?

options.A: Two copies, one from each parent
options.B: Only one copy from the father
options.D: Only one copy from the mother

explanation: Autosomal recessive disorders require both parents to pass on a copy of the altered gene for the child to be affected. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h2)

question: Why are males more commonly affected by X-linked recessive disorders than females?

options.A: The Y chromosome protects female offspring
options.B: Males possess only one X chromosome
options.C: X chromosomes only exist in male bodies
options.D: Females do not have any chromosomes

explanation: Since males only have one X chromosome, a single recessive mutation on that chromosome will express the disease, whereas females have a backup X chromosome. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h2)

question: What is the minimum number of generations a nurse should typically explore when taking a family health history?
explanation: Looking back across three generations (parents, children, and grandparents) helps reveal hidden inheritance patterns of hereditary conditions. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h3)

question: A young couple visits the clinic and mentions that multiple relatives on both sides died young from the same rare heart condition. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Prescribe blood pressure medication for both partners
options.B: Construct a pedigree chart and refer them for genetic assessment
options.C: Advise them to change their cooking oil immediately
options.D: Tell them not to worry because heart disease is completely normal

explanation: A pattern of early-onset disease in multiple relatives is a major red flag requiring formal genetic risk evaluation. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h3)

question: What is the primary benefit of pre-conception genetic screening?

options.A: It allows couples to know their carrier status before pregnancy
options.B: It replaces the need for standard antenatal care
options.C: It immediately cures any existing genetic mutations
options.D: It guarantees that a child will never fall sick

explanation: Pre-conception screening reveals if partners carry matching recessive genes, helping them make informed family planning decisions. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h4)

question: Which of the following describes a key difference between screening tests and diagnostic tests in prenatal care?

options.A: Screening tests estimate risk, while diagnostic tests confirm a condition
options.B: Diagnostic tests are performed on every single pregnant woman
options.C: Screening tests are only done after birth
options.D: Screening tests use surgery, while diagnostic tests are painless

explanation: Screening tests only show the probability or risk of a disorder, whereas diagnostic tests provide a definitive diagnosis. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h4)

question: What is the teach-back method used for during patient education?

options.A: Writing prescription notes for the pharmacist
options.B: Asking the patient to explain the information back in their own words
options.C: Having the nurse read the textbook out loud to the patient
options.D: Testing the nurse's ability to memorize medical terminology

explanation: The teach-back method checks whether the patient truly understood the instructions by having them repeat the information. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h5)

question: Why must a nurse maintain neutrality when counseling patients about genetic risks?

options.A: To allow patients to make their own choices based on personal values
options.B: To prevent patients from asking questions about their family
options.C: To prove that genetics has no real impact on health
options.D: To ensure the hospital avoids paying for laboratory tests

explanation: Reproductive decisions are deeply personal; nurses must guide without imposing personal beliefs or forcing specific choices. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical responsibility of the nurse regarding genetic test results?

options.B: Respecting the autonomy of the patient in decision-making
options.C: Sharing the results openly with extended family members without consent
options.D: Maintaining strict patient confidentiality to prevent discrimination

explanation: Nurses must protect patient privacy and confidentiality; sharing genetic results without explicit consent violates ethical standards. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h6)

question: How should a nurse handle cultural beliefs that attribute hereditary conditions solely to spiritual curses?

options.A: Publicly ridicule the family for holding traditional beliefs
options.B: Refuse to treat patients who mention spiritual explanations
options.C: Agree with the curse theory to avoid arguing with patients
options.D: Provide gentle, respectful education while addressing community myths

explanation: Nurses can bridge traditional beliefs and medical science through respectful education and community sensitization rather than harsh judgment. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h6)

question: Who typically acts as the central coordinator connecting various specialists and the patient in clinical settings?
explanation: Nurses coordinate care pathways, schedule referrals, and bridge communication between patients and the multidisciplinary healthcare team. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h7)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for managing hereditary conditions?

options.A: It removes the need for nurses to speak directly with patients
options.B: Hospital regulations require at least ten staff members for every patient
options.C: No single profession has all the skills needed to address complex genetic and social needs
options.D: It ensures that laboratory scientists make all final clinical decisions

explanation: Hereditary conditions involve medical, emotional, and social challenges that require diverse expertise from multiple healthcare professionals. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h7)
